description: Verify that TCP in SYN-SENT drops a segment with neither SYN nor RST and remains in the same state (RFC 793 §3.9 p68). 2 iterations exercise stp ∈ {no data, data}
approach:
[Objective]
A bare ACK (or ACK+payload) in SYN-SENT is meaningless — DUT hasn't established sequence numbers yet. RFC 793 §3.9 says drop, no response.

[Scenario — chronological]
Two iterations:
• Phase 1: tester emits bare ACK with acceptable ack.
• Phase 2: tester emits ACK+payload with acceptable ack.
For each: DUT must not respond.

[Pass condition]
No DUT response in either phase.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_p<n>_no_dut_syn — phase n SYN missing
• Fail_p<n>_unexpected_response — phase n DUT responded

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped bare ACK and ACK+payload in SYN-SENT — normal
verdicts.Fail_p1_no_dut_syn: No DUT SYN phase 1 bare ACK
verdicts.Fail_p1_unexpected_response: DUT emitted response to bare ACK with acceptable ack
verdicts.Fail_p2_no_dut_syn: No DUT SYN phase 2 ACK with payload
verdicts.Fail_p2_unexpected_response: DUT emitted response to ACK with payload acceptable ack
